NovaLink Mobile -- Consumer Contract Terms, Section 7 (Early Termination)

7.1 Customers on a 24-month contract who terminate the agreement before the end of the
term pay an Early Termination Fee (ETF) of $15 for each month remaining in the contract
term.
7.2 No ETF applies if the customer terminates within the first 14 days after activation
(buyer's remorse period).
7.3 Exception overriding 7.1: if NovaLink increases the customer's base monthly plan
price by more than 5%, any customer who terminates within 60 days of the price-increase
notice owes no ETF, regardless of how many months remain on the contract.
7.4 Military deployment exception, taking priority over 7.1 and 7.3: an active-duty
customer deployed for 90 days or more may terminate with no ETF upon submitting deployment
orders.
7.5 Where an ETF is owed, it is capped at $300 total regardless of months remaining.

Account file -- Maria Ionescu, account #NL-88213

Maria signed a 24-month contract on January 10, 2025, and her line was activated the same
day. On July 1, 2026, NovaLink raised the base price of her plan by 8% and mailed the
required price-increase notice that same day. Maria is not in the military. On August 10,
2026, Maria called customer service and requested to cancel her contract effective
immediately.

Agent note: "Confirmed account is not on a corporate plan, not a military exception case.
Customer cited the price increase as her reason for leaving. Referencing the notice sent
7/1/2026 and comparing to today's cancellation date."

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Maria owe an early termination fee?
questions.notes: 8% increase >5% threshold; cancelled Aug 10 is 40 days after Jul 1 notice, within 60 -> 7.3 waives ETF, overrides 7.1.

questions.instruction: Which section of the policy determines the outcome of Maria's cancellation request?

candidates.description: 7.1: the standard per-month ETF applies
7.2: she is within the 14-day buyer's remorse period
7.3: the price-increase exception waives the ETF
7.4: the military deployment exception waives the ETF

questions.notes: Price rose 8% (>5%) and she cancelled within 60 days of the notice -> 7.3 governs, not 7.1/7.2/7.4.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Maria's cancellation?

candidates.description: She cancelled within 14 days of activation
The plan price increase exceeded 5%
She cancelled within 60 days of the price-increase notice
She qualifies for the military deployment exception
Her ETF was reduced by the $300 cap

questions.notes: 8%>5% and Aug10 is 40 days after Jul1 (both true); not remorse period, not military, and no ETF was owed so the cap is moot.

questions.instruction: Based on the contract terms, will NovaLink charge Maria anything for cancelling when she did?
questions.notes: Same as Q1 reworded: price-increase exception (7.3) waives any charge.

PeakFit Gym Membership Agreement, Section 5 (Freeze & Cancellation)

5.1 Members may freeze their membership for a fee of $10/month, minimum 1 month, maximum
3 consecutive months per calendar year.
5.2 Medical freeze exception: with a doctor's note, the freeze fee is waived and the
freeze may extend up to 6 months.
5.3 Cancellation requires 30 days' written notice. Members on a 12-month commitment plan
who cancel before completing 12 months owe an early cancellation fee of $50, UNLESS the
cancellation is due to the member relocating more than 50 miles from the nearest PeakFit
location (the relocation exception), in which case no fee applies but proof of the new
address is required.
5.4 Members cancelling under a valid exception (medical or relocation) after paying annual
dues upfront receive a prorated refund equal to $1/12 of the annual dues for each full
unused month remaining in the term; partial months are not refunded.
5.5 Members who signed up through an employer/corporate partner discount program are not
eligible for the relocation exception in 5.3 and must pay the $50 fee plus forfeit any
remaining prepaid discount balance.

Membership file -- Diego Fuentes, member #PF-40217

Diego signed up directly (not through any employer program) for a 12-month commitment
beginning March 1, 2026, and ending February 28, 2027, paying $480 upfront ($40/month).
On September 15, 2026, Diego requested cancellation, explaining that he accepted a new job
120 miles from his current city and is moving. He attached a copy of his new lease,
dated September 10, 2026, listing the new address.

Front-desk log: "Verified lease document matches the address Diego gave us. Six full
months of the term have elapsed (March through August); September is only half over."

questions.instruction: Under this policy, must Diego pay the $50 early cancellation fee?
questions.notes: 120 miles exceeds the 50-mile relocation threshold and proof was provided, so the 5.3 relocation exception waives the fee.

questions.instruction: How much prorated refund is Diego entitled to for unused prepaid dues?

candidates.description: $0 -- no refund is owed
$200 -- five unused full months at $40 each
$240 -- six unused full months at $40 each
$480 -- the full annual amount

questions.notes: 12 months at $40 each; 6 full months used (Mar-Aug), September is only partial and unrefunded, leaving 5 full unused months x $40 = $200.

questions.instruction: Which of the following apply to Diego's cancellation?

candidates.description: The relocation exception in 5.3 applies
He used the medical freeze exception
He signed up through an employer/corporate program
The $50 cancellation fee is waived
He provided proof of his new address
He is entitled to a prorated refund of prepaid dues

questions.notes: Relocation (120mi), proof (lease) and fee waiver all apply and entitle him to the 5.4 refund; not medical, not corporate.

Brightwater University Library -- Circulation Policy, Section 3

3.1 Standard loan period for undergraduates: 21 days for general circulation books.
3.2 Graduate students: 90 days for general circulation books.
3.3 Faculty: 180 days.
3.4 Items may be renewed twice, each renewal granting another full loan period, UNLESS
the item has been recalled by another patron, in which case it must be returned within 7
days of the recall notice regardless of the remaining loan time or renewals available.
3.5 Overdue fines: $0.25/day for undergraduates, $0.50/day for graduate students; faculty
owe no overdue fines but lose borrowing privileges after 14 days overdue on any item.
3.6 Reserve/course-reserve items have a 2-hour loan and are never eligible for renewal,
including under 3.4.
3.7 Fines are capped at $20 per item for students.

candidates.description: $20.00 (the cap)

questions.notes: Recall deadline was Nov 12; returned Nov 20 = 8 days late x $0.50 (graduate rate) = $4.00, well under the $20 cap.

3.1 Standard loan period for undergraduates: 21 days for general circulation books.

3.3 Faculty: 180 days.
3.4 Items may be renewed twice, each renewal granting another full loan period, UNLESS

3.8 Undergraduate and graduate students whose accounts accrue more than $20 in unpaid

(ILL) privileges suspended until the balance is paid in full. This account-wide rule
applies to students only.

Hi Priya,

I checked your account in detail. You currently have two overdue general-circulation
books, each carrying an $11.00 fine, for $22.00 in unpaid fines total across your
account. Neither individual item has hit the $20-per-item cap in section 3.7 on its own
($11 each), but section 3.8 looks at the account total, not individual items, and your
combined total of $22.00 is over the $20 threshold in 3.8. That's why both your general
borrowing privileges and your ILL privileges are currently suspended -- the suspension
will lift automatically once the $22.00 balance is paid.

Regarding Professor Okafor: he's right that faculty are never charged overdue fines under
3.5. However, that same section also says faculty who are more than 14 days overdue on
any item lose their borrowing privileges, separately from any fine. So his account is
also currently restricted, just under a completely different rule than yours -- his is a
time-based borrowing restriction with no dollar amount attached, not a fine-based
suspension, and section 3.8's account-wide fine rule doesn't apply to faculty at all.

Let me know once you've paid down the balance and I'll lift the hold right away.

Best,
Marcus

WheelGo Car Rental -- Rental Terms, Section 6 (Drivers & Damage Coverage)

6.1 Renters aged 21-24 incur a Young Driver Surcharge of $25/day. Renters under 21 may
not rent except under the corporate account exception in 6.5.
6.2 Renters aged 25 and older incur no young driver surcharge.
6.3 Collision Damage Waiver (CDW), optional at $18/day, covers all collision damage
except: (a) damage incurred off paved roads, (b) damage incurred while any driver on the
agreement is impaired, and (c) tire, undercarriage, or windshield damage under $250,
which the renter is always responsible for regardless of CDW.
6.4 If CDW is purchased and the renter is enrolled in the WheelGo Elite loyalty tier, the
6.3(c) exclusion is fully waived: Elite+CDW covers everything CDW normally excludes,
except (a) and (b), which are never covered.
6.5 Corporate account exception: renters aged 18-20 may rent if the reservation is booked
under a registered corporate account and a manager pre-authorization code is provided;
the young driver surcharge for this group is $35/day.

The door dent is covered

pays return shipping only if the reason is "item not as described" or "defective."

City of Rivendale -- Special Event & Noise Permit Code, Section 12

12.1 Amplified sound events on public property require a Noise Permit if the sound will
be audible more than 100 feet from the source. Fee: $75 for events under 4 hours, $150
for events 4-8 hours, $300 for events over 8 hours.
12.2 Events expecting more than 200 attendees additionally require a Special Event Permit
($200 flat), regardless of noise.
12.3 Nonprofit organizations registered with the city receive a 50% discount on the Noise
Permit fee only (not the Special Event Permit fee) when the event is free to the public.
12.4 Permit applications must be submitted at least 21 days before the event date. Fewer
than 21 days' notice adds a $100 rush fee to the total, UNLESS the applicant is a
city-recognized emergency/relief organization.
12.5 No permit is required for events held entirely indoors with sound not audible
outside the building.

City of Rivendale -- Building & Zoning Code, Section 20 (Minor Work Exemptions)

20.1 A building permit is required for any structural alteration, electrical work beyond
like-for-like fixture replacement, or plumbing work beyond fixture replacement.
20.2 Exempt from permit requirements: fences under 6 feet tall, painting, flooring, and
non-structural interior cosmetic work. (Fences 6 feet or taller are not exempt.)
20.3 Detached accessory structures (sheds, detached garages) under 120 square feet do NOT
require a building permit, UNLESS they include plumbing or electrical wiring, in which
case a permit IS required regardless of the structure's size.
20.4 Homeowners performing their own work on their primary residence ("owner-builder") do
not need a contractor's license, but must still obtain any permit that is otherwise
required before starting work.

Permit inquiry form -- submitted by Greg Hastings, homeowner

"I'm putting up a detached storage shed in my backyard, 96 square feet, on my primary
residence. I'll be doing the work myself. My electrician buddy is going to help out too,
since it's not like the shed won't have a light switch and an outlet wired in -- of
course it will, I want to be able to see in there at night. Separately, I'm also planning
to put up a new fence along the side yard sometime this fall, still deciding on the exact
height."

Office note: "Applicant did not submit a separate electrical permit request; treating the
wiring as part of the same shed project for now."

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Greg's shed require a building permit?
questions.notes: The double negative ('not like...won't have...wired in') confirms the shed WILL have electrical wiring; 20.3 requires a permit for any wired accessory structure regardless of the 120 sq ft size exemption.

questions.instruction: What is the permit status of Greg's planned fence under this policy?

candidates.description: Exempt -- no permit needed, the fence is under 6 feet
A permit is required -- the fence is 6 feet or taller
Cannot be determined from the information given

questions.notes: The exemption in 20.2 turns on fence height, which Greg explicitly says he hasn't decided yet -- a required fact is missing.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Greg's shed project?

candidates.description: The shed is under 120 square feet
A building permit is required for the shed
Greg needs a contractor's license to do the work
The shed will have electrical wiring
The planned fence's height was specified

questions.notes: 96 sqft (<120) but wired -> permit required despite the size exemption; owner-builder needs no license (20.4); fence height was left undecided.

Aegis Appliance Warranty -- Tier Terms

Standard (included free, years 1 only): covers parts and labor for manufacturing defects
only. Does not cover accidental damage, water damage, or cosmetic issues.
Extended (+$49 at purchase, extends coverage through year 3 total): same defect coverage
as Standard, PLUS one-time accidental damage coverage (capped at $200) available only
during year 2 or year 3 of ownership, not year 1.
Premium (+$129 at purchase, extends coverage through year 5 total): covers manufacturing
defects, unlimited accidental damage (no cap), and water damage, for the full 5 years
including year 1.
Cross-tier rule: coverage under any tier is void if the product was purchased from an
unauthorized third-party reseller; an authorized-retailer receipt is required for any
claim.

Claim file -- Lindsey Cho, refrigerator model AX-400

Purchased May 1, 2023, from an authorized Aegis retailer (receipt on file). Extended
warranty purchased at the same time. On June 10, 2026, Lindsey filed a claim: she dropped
a toolbox on the unit, denting and cracking the front panel. Repair estimate: $150. This
is her first-ever claim on this unit.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Lindsey's accidental damage claim covered?
questions.notes: Extended covers only through year 3 (May 2023-May 2026); the June 10, 2026 claim falls in year 4, after Extended's coverage ended.

questions.instruction: Which warranty tier, if any, would have covered this claim on this date?

candidates.description: Standard would have covered it
Her current Extended warranty covers it
Only Premium would have covered it
No tier would have covered it

questions.notes: Standard never covers accidental damage; Extended maxes out at year 3; only Premium's unlimited, 5-year accidental damage coverage reaches year 4.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Lindsey's coverage situation?

candidates.description: The unit was purchased from an authorized retailer
She purchased the Extended warranty
Her claim falls within Extended's accidental-damage window
Her claim would be covered if she had Premium
Her claim would be covered under Standard

questions.notes: Authorized purchase and Extended ownership are both true; her year-4 claim is outside Extended's window but within Premium's; Standard never covers accidental damage.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, would Lindsey's claim have been covered if she had purchased Premium instead of Extended?
questions.notes: Premium covers unlimited accidental damage for all 5 years including year 1, so a year-4 claim would fall within its coverage.

state:
VoyageGuard Travel Insurance Certificate, Section 8 (Trip Cancellation)

8.1 The trip cancellation benefit reimburses 100% of prepaid, non-refundable trip costs
(up to a $10,000 policy maximum) when the trip is cancelled for a covered reason,
including the insured's own sudden illness or a documented change in a medical condition
on a doctor's advice.
8.2 Pre-existing medical conditions are excluded from coverage UNLESS: (a) the policy was
purchased within 14 days of the initial trip deposit, AND (b) as of the purchase date, the
traveler was medically stable with no new diagnosis or treatment change. This is the
pre-existing condition waiver, and both parts are assessed as of the purchase date.
8.3 Cancel-for-any-reason (CFAR) is available only as a separate paid upgrade purchased
within 21 days of the initial deposit, and reimburses 75% of prepaid costs.
8.4 Claims filed after the scheduled departure date are not eligible for trip cancellation
benefits.

Claim file -- Anita Desai, policy #VG-33012

Trip deposit paid: January 5, 2026 ($4,000, non-refundable). VoyageGuard policy purchased:
January 15, 2026. Anita did not purchase the CFAR upgrade. Anita has a documented
pre-existing heart condition, diagnosed in 2019 and stable since, with no treatment
changes as of January 15, 2026.

Scheduled departure: April 10, 2026. On March 1, 2026, Anita's cardiologist changed her
medication following a checkup that found a shift in her condition. Anita cancelled the
trip on March 3, 2026, on her cardiologist's advice, and filed her claim the same day.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does the pre-existing condition exclusion bar Anita's claim?
questions.notes: The waiver test in 8.2 looks at her status as of the Jan 15 purchase date (stable, no treatment change yet); the March treatment change doesn't retroactively void it.

questions.instruction: How much is Anita entitled to receive for her cancelled trip?

candidates.description: $3,000 -- 75% under CFAR
$4,000 -- 100% of the deposit
$10,000 -- the policy maximum

questions.notes: Standard cancellation benefit is 100% of the $4,000 deposit; she never purchased CFAR, so the 75% figure doesn't apply; well under the $10,000 max.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Anita's policy and claim?

candidates.description: The policy was purchased within 14 days of the trip deposit
She was medically stable as of the purchase date
She purchased the CFAR upgrade
Her claim was filed before the scheduled departure date
The pre-existing condition exclusion applies to her claim

questions.notes: 10 days between deposit and purchase, stable as of purchase, and claim filed a month before departure are all true; no CFAR, and the exclusion is waived.

VoyageGuard Travel Insurance Certificate, Section 11 (Baggage Delay)

11.1 If checked baggage is delayed more than 12 hours, the policy reimburses receipted
essential-item purchases (clothing, toiletries) up to $100 for the first 24 hours of
delay, and up to $50 for each additional 24-hour period, to a maximum of $300 total.
11.2 Unreceipted claims are reimbursed at a flat $25 regardless of delay length.
11.3 This benefit does not apply to the final return leg home -- only to the outbound
trip or connections before reaching the final destination.
11.4 If baggage is declared permanently lost rather than delayed, Section 12 (Baggage
Loss) applies instead of this section.

Claim file -- Ben Okoro, policy #VG-40871

Ben's checked bag was delayed 48 hours on his outbound flight, before he reached his
destination hotel. The airline confirmed the bag as delayed, not lost, and it was
eventually delivered to his hotel. Ben kept all receipts: $90 spent on essentials in the
first 24 hours of the delay, and $60 spent in the second 24-hour period.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Ben's baggage delay claim eligible under Section 11?
questions.notes: The bag was delayed (not lost) more than 12 hours on the outbound leg, so Section 11 applies -- not Section 12, and not the return-leg exclusion.

questions.instruction: How much is Ben entitled to for his essential-item purchases?
questions.notes: $90 (first 24h, under the $100 cap) + $50 (second 24h, $60 actual capped at $50) = $140.

Meridian Corp Employee Handbook, Section 14 (Paid Time Off)

14.1 PTO accrues monthly based on tenure: 0-2 years = 1.25 days/month (15 days/year);
2-5 years = 1.67 days/month (20 days/year); 5+ years = 2.08 days/month (25 days/year).
14.2 A new tenure-tier rate takes effect starting the month AFTER the employee's
anniversary date -- not during the anniversary month itself.
14.3 Unused PTO carries over into the next calendar year up to a maximum of 5 days;
anything above 5 days remaining on December 31 is forfeited, with no cash-out, unless the
employee works in a state with a mandatory PTO payout law (listed in Appendix C).
14.4 Part-time employees (under 30 hours/week) accrue PTO at (hours/40) times the
applicable full-time rate.

Employee file -- Farid Nasser, full-time, hired March 15, 2021

Farid's 5-year anniversary is March 15, 2026. He works in a state that is not listed in
Appendix C (no mandatory PTO payout law applies to him). On December 31, 2025, Farid had
7 unused PTO days remaining. As of October 2026, Farid is still employed full-time in the
same role.

HR note: "Confirming Farid's tier transition date for payroll -- his old rate was 1.67
days/month under the 2-5 year tier."

questions.instruction: Under this policy, did Farid's accrual rate increase to 2.08 days/month starting in March 2026, his anniversary month?
questions.notes: 14.2 starts the new tier the month AFTER the anniversary month; March is the anniversary month itself, so the old 1.67 rate still applied then; 2.08 started in April.

questions.instruction: How many of Farid's unused 2025 PTO days carried over into 2026?

candidates.description: 0 days
2 days
5 days
7 days

questions.notes: 7 unused days, but the carryover cap is 5 (14.3); the remaining 2 are forfeited since no mandatory payout law applies to him.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Farid's PTO as of October 2026?

candidates.description: He is in the 5+ year accrual tier
He accrues 2.08 days per month
He is eligible to cash out his forfeited 2025 days
He is a part-time employee
He carried over 5 days of PTO into 2026

questions.notes: By October he's well past the April tier change and accrues 2.08/month; carried over the 5-day cap; not part-time; no payout law applies so no cash-out.

Meridian Corp Employee Handbook, Section 16 (Parental Leave)

16.1 Full-time employees with at least 12 consecutive months of employment are eligible
for 12 weeks of paid parental leave at 100% of base salary, for birth, adoption, or foster
placement.
16.2 Full-time employees with 3-12 months of employment are eligible for 6 weeks at 50%
of base salary.
16.3 Employees with under 3 months of employment are not eligible for paid parental leave
under this policy.
16.4 Independent contractors and interns are not eligible for parental leave benefits
under this policy, regardless of tenure.
16.5 Pregnancy complications requiring medical leave before birth are covered under the
separate Short-Term Disability policy (Section 17), not counted against the 16.1/16.2
parental leave allotment.
16.6 Both parents employed at Meridian may each independently claim their own full
entitlement under 16.1/16.2; one parent's leave does not reduce the other's.

HR memo -- parental leave eligibility review, Reeves household

Jamal Reeves: full-time software engineer, hired 4 years ago. Spouse Priya Reeves:
full-time designer, hired 7 months ago. Both are expecting a child together and have both
filed for parental leave.

Separate internal chat, HR helpdesk channel:

Sam Delacroix: "hey, I've been on a 2-year independent contractor engagement here, longer
than plenty of the full-timers honestly. My partner and I are having a baby in the spring,
can I get paid parental leave like everyone else?"

HR (Denise): "I checked with Sam directly -- his engagement is structured as an
independent contractor arrangement, not employment, so section 16.4 excludes him from
parental leave benefits regardless of how long the engagement has run."

Sam Delacroix: "Oh sure, TWO YEARS of me being here basically full time and I get nothing
because of a paperwork label. Great policy, really generous of you all."

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Sam entitled to paid parental leave?
questions.notes: 16.4 excludes independent contractors regardless of tenure; Sam's 2-year engagement length is irrelevant, and his sarcasm doesn't change the outcome.

questions.instruction: What is Priya's parental leave entitlement under this policy?

candidates.description: 12 weeks at 100% of base salary
6 weeks at 50% of base salary
Not eligible for paid parental leave
Short-Term Disability coverage only

questions.notes: Priya has 7 months of tenure, placing her in the 3-12 month tier (16.2: 6 weeks at 50%), not Jamal's 12-week/100% tier (16.1, 4 years tenure).

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Jamal's approved parental leave reduce the number of weeks Priya is entitled to?
questions.notes: 16.6 states each parent independently claims their own entitlement; one spouse's leave does not reduce the other's.
